title: Windows dv-harness CLI adapter: 3 real bugs blocking every run-stage call
symptoms: run-stage crashes with FileNotFoundError (WinError 2) even though `claude --version` works fine interactively
run-stage crashes with UnicodeDecodeError / AttributeError('NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip') after the FileNotFoundError is fixed
run-stage fails with 'Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print' after both prior fixes
root_cause: dv_harness/adapters/cli.py's ClaudeCLIAdapter.run() had 3 independent Windows-specific bugs, each only reachable after fixing the previous one: (1) subprocess.run(['claude', ...], shell=False) calls Win32 CreateProcess directly, which does not do PATHEXT resolution -- it could only ever find the non-executable POSIX shell script `claude` npm installs alongside the real `claude.cmd` launcher. (2) text=True without an explicit encoding decodes the child's stdout/stderr using locale.getpreferredencoding(), which resolves to cp950 on a zh-TW Windows machine, not UTF-8 -- claude's own UTF-8 JSON output crashes the reader thread. (3) claude's own --help confirms `-p`/`--print` is a bare flag and `prompt` is a separate positional argument, but the resolved command is `claude.cmd`, a cmd.exe batch-file shim whose argument forwarding is line-oriented -- a real multi-line stage prompt (build_stage_prompt() output, confirmed live at 6227 chars with embedded \n) silently truncated/broke when placed on the command line.
fix: (1) resolve the configured command via shutil.which() before subprocess.run() (real PATHEXT resolution on Windows, safe no-op on POSIX). (2) pass encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' explicitly to subprocess.run(), plus `(p.stdout or '')`/`(p.stderr or '')` defensive guards. (3) never place `prompt` on the command line -- keep `-p` as a bare flag and pipe the prompt via subprocess.run()'s `input=` parameter instead, which uses a real OS pipe with no batch-file/cmd.exe argument parsing involved at all.

verification.regression: dv_harness_tests/ full suite green throughout (1682+ tests) -- none of these 3 bugs were ever visible to the test suite, only to a real subprocess launch on this real OS
verification.reaudit: CONFIRMED: after all 3 fixes, a real `dv-harness run-stage --stage ENV_CHECK` completed end-to-end with a real PASS verdict

note: Commits: d46f3c2 (shutil.which), e20034f (UTF-8 encoding), 45ff72b (stdin piping). IMPORTANT for future sessions on this same Windows dev machine: if `dv-harness run-stage` ever fails again with any of the 3 symptoms above, these fixes are already in dv_harness/adapters/cli.py -- check `git log -- dv_harness/adapters/cli.py` first before re-diagnosing from scratch. For a DIFFERENT machine/OS, these are still the first 3 things to check for CLI-adapter failures: command resolution, stdout/stderr encoding, and how the prompt reaches the child process.
provenance: dv-agent-harness-l5-7a session, 2026-09-01, live dv-harness run-stage debugging
